title: Outcome-based work arrangements instead of time-based models
asked: Ms Valerie Lee asked whether the Ministry of Manpower has studied ways to encourage outcome-based work arrangements rather than structured time-based models, and what measures support employers and employees in adopting them while protecting productivity and well-being.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said outcome-based work can benefit employers and employees where the job allows, but may not suit shift work or roles needing a physical presence, and that many PMEs already work on delivering outcomes with limited tracking of hours. He cited the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, under which employers consider requests on reasonable business grounds and outcomes and tracking are mutually agreed, plus government support for technology adoption and job redesign through enterprise and workforce transformation initiatives. He also pointed to the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces, including not requiring employees to respond to non-urgent work messages until the following working day.

key_points.point: Outcome-based arrangements may not suit jobs requiring shift work or a physical presence.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: such a model may not be suitable for jobs that would require shift work or a physical presence

key_points.point: Many professionals, managers and executives already work on delivering outcomes with limited tracking of work hours.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Many professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) already work on the basis of delivering successful outcomes with limited tracking of work hours.

key_points.point: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests set out the request process and require employers to consider requests on reasonable business grounds, with outcomes and tracking mutually agreed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests sets out the process for workers to formally request for flexible work arrangements and for employers to consider these requests on reasonable business grounds.

key_points.point: The Government supports employers in adopting technology and redesigning jobs through enterprise and workforce transformation initiatives.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The Government also supports employers in adopting technology and redesigning jobs through enterprise and workforce transformation initiatives

key_points.point: The Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces sets out good practices, such as not requiring responses to non-urgent work messages until the next working day.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Such practices could include not requiring employees to respond to non-urgent work-related messages and emails until the following working day.

key_points.point: There is no specific Ministry study measuring outcomes between flexible work arrangements and key performance; NTUC and worker survey results rank flexible work arrangements first among preferred requirements, ahead of other leave and financial contributions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: flexible work arrangements are ranked number one in terms of preferred requirements, compared to other leave and even financial contributions

key_points.point: Determining best performance and value for money is left to the market and employers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: we leave it to the market and also the employers to determine what is the best performance and what is value for money

key_points.point: Within Government there is a range of roles, and supervisors manage staff and how they deliver outcomes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: we leave it to the supervisors to manage the staff and how they deliver those outcomes

key_points.point: Autonomous universities decide how they determine outcomes and performance, and can approach TAFEP, the Institute for Human Resource Professionals or NTUC for help.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: We leave it to the universities to decide how they determine outcomes and performance

left_open: Whether the Ministry has set any targets or metrics for productivity under outcome-based work arrangements
Whether the Government monitors flexible work practices at Government-affiliated institutions such as autonomous universities
supplementary: Whether evidence links flexible work to productivity, and whether the public service and autonomous universities apply outcome-based performance management
